SEQ-A00.why: Within one assembly the ops follow the fixed op order (plates, studs, openings, bracing, cap / sill, rim, joists / ridge, rafters, ties); used when the op-specific rule does not apply because an op is absent.

SEQ-F01.why: Rims and joists bear on sills and beams.

SEQ-F02.why: Rims carry the joist layout and hold joists upright.

SEQ-W01.why: Studs are nailed between laid-out plates.

SEQ-W02.why: Jacks and headers fasten to the king studs.

SEQ-W03.why: Bracing goes into a complete, plumbed wall.

SEQ-W04.why: Cap plates lap over intersecting walls, so every wall on the level must stand first.

SEQ-W05.why: As SEQ-W04 for walls with openings.

SEQ-S01.why: Stairs after the storey is closed in.

SEQ-W06.why: Exterior walls first square and stiffen the deck; partitions fit between them.

SEQ-X01.why: Walls are framed on the finished deck of their level (platform framing).

SEQ-X02.why: The upper floor bears on the completed (capped) walls below; plan fall protection before joist work at height.

SEQ-X03.why: Upper-storey walls (balloon or platform) bear on completed walls below.

SEQ-X05.why: Roof framing bears on completed top-storey walls.

SEQ-X06.why: Ceiling joists/top floor tie the wall tops before rafters thrust on them.
